Byron Donalds.quote_or_summary: Economic Club of Miami interview (Justin Sayfie): "I think the future of the state, what's going to be important are data centers and power." and "We need to embrace that, not run away from that." (Quotes as reported by Orlando Weekly and WLRN; the video itself could not be viewed/transcribed.)

Same June 2025 quotes, corroborated by WLRN; video is titled 'Florida's Economic Future: A Conversation with Byron Donalds, Economic Club of Miami, Downtown Miami' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4vTl9LhcmFk).

Voted for the House version of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which included a 10-year moratorium on state and local regulation of AI systems (preempting local/state limits); Senate removed it. In Sept 2026 at a TPUSA meeting at UCF he said: "That's one provision that I wasn't probably the biggest fan of."

Opposes a statewide data-center moratorium. At a Clearwater event: New York's moratorium is "a signal to the business community that this is not a place to invest capital." Says he favors slowing construction of new data centers, with balance; "In the state of Florida, utility bills for Floridians will not go up if a hyperscale data center is built." Dismissed Jolly's one-year moratorium as 'politics'.

MIXED: Backs state law SB 484 (signed May 2026; data centers pay own costs, consumptive-use permits, local authority preserved) as "a really strong step in the right direction"; "If local governments don't want them, they won't build them, and that's just the way it is." Campaign: "If communities don't want data centers, there will be no data centers in those communities." To News4JAX: "County commissioners issue building permits, not governors." Says he would release the state data-center study due June 1, 2027.

Introduced federal 'Protecting the Ratepayers Act' (July 2026) requiring data-center operators to get all energy and water from sources that do not use or affect the grid or public water systems (as summarized by Orlando Weekly, citing donalds.house.gov DocumentID=2635; bill text not read).

CONTEXT, not a stance: Politico reported (July 20, 2026) Donalds received dozens of contributions from AI interests, including companies seeking to build hyperscale data centers in Florida. Politico page could not be fetched; relayed via Orlando Weekly. Wikipedia states he 'supports expanding development of data centers in Florida'. Jolly's ad calls him 'Data Center Donalds'.

On growth generally: favors continued growth under the existing permitting framework ("We are going to maintain that"; "This is not a new phenomenon"); cites Space Coast commercial space as an economic opportunity (News4JAX paraphrase). No documented position found from him on farmland protection, rural-lands bills (SB 686) or growth management.

In campaign ads he pledged to protect Floridians from AI data centers that would 'jack up' utility rates; fight for a ratepayer-protection plan; opposes a statewide ban or state preemption; cities and counties keep full authority over whether a facility belongs in their community (ClickOrlando voter guide).

Calls for a 'streamlined' state permitting office for major developments, permits on an open state website 'with a ticking clock', and modernized permitting for new home construction (ClickOrlando voter guide). Also favors continued growth under existing permitting framework (News4JAX, Oct 6 2026).

Same June 2025 Economic Club of Miami interview, per J.C. Bruce Substack summary: he said Florida has available land and could build such facilities while keeping the state's natural beauty. (Secondary summary of the video, not a transcript.)

Leading the Future, a pro-AI super PAC funded by figures including OpenAI president Greg Brockman and Andreessen Horowitz founders, pledged about $5 million to help Donalds (first gubernatorial candidate it backed). His strategist Ryan Smith: "America must lead in the AI space"; Donalds would be a 'standard-bearer for responsible innovation while also protecting Floridians.' Donalds himself not quoted; campaign did not comment.

Fox 13 (Sept 28 2026): opposes statewide pause - a moratorium signals Florida is "not a place to invest capital"; "we require water permits for these centers so that we protect Florida's aquifers"; "no more NDAs" on local proposals; 'dovish on solar and wind' and proposes four data centers on a solar array powered by a small modular reactor. Notes Avila's earlier bill to exempt data-center plans from public-records laws failed; article doesn't say whether Donalds backed it.

Fox 13 interview with Craig Patrick (Oct 31 2026, via Yahoo): "It is now state law in Florida that if local governments say no data center, then no data centers." Says 27 counties/municipalities have issued a moratorium or ban (about three outright bans); state study due June 1 2027; of Jolly's statewide moratorium: "If he wants to be governor, he should actually read the law." Fox 35 (Sept 17): "We're not going to preempt local governments"; "these are their communities, they're the ones that have to make these final decisions." Mother Jones (Oct 15 2026) headline: 'Byron Donalds is pro-data centers. So is his stock portfolio' (article not retrievable).

Fox 13 interview Oct 31 2026: "It can't take two years to put a shovel in the ground"; citing a National Association of Home Builders study, "we need to reform that system" (permitting and timelines); "The way we raise additional tax dollars is we have a thriving and growing economy." ClickOrlando guide: 'streamlined' state permitting office for major developments, a 'ticking clock' on permits.

Mother Jones: he told a group of Miami businesses that Florida was 'wide open' for development (article's wording) and said: "We have actual land in our state that is still pristine, available to use." (Mother Jones says 'last spring'; exact date and venue not given, may be the Economic Club of Miami appearance.) This is the closest documented statement tying data centers to using undeveloped land.

Mother Jones: at an August 2026 campaign event, attacking Jolly's moratorium: "There ain't no bans coming"; moratorium proposals 'sound good on TV' or social media. Also: Politico (July 2026) reported four developers 'actively pursuing or had previously proposed data centers' among his donors; his Aug 2026 disclosure lists up to $390,000 in stocks tied to data-center companies (Microsoft, Amazon, Monolithic Power Systems) managed by Moran Wealth Management; his campaign war chest is $125M.

David Jolly.quote_or_summary: Promises a one-year statewide moratorium on new hyperscale data centers: "I'll issue a moratorium on my very first day in office." Says buildout "is moving too quickly."

At Lakeland event: "Big tech is coming in before we can get the appropriate environmental regulations in place"; "The labor and economic impact is not worth the investment that we make." Immediate moratorium.

CNN interview: "If Florida's not a place for the big data centers because of our fragile water infrastructure, it's okay to say that." Florida Phoenix headline (Sept 18): 'David Jolly: A complete ban on data centers in Florida should be on the table' (article itself returned 403; headline only).
Would 'invest in smart growth' and work to restore local Home Rule (ClickOrlando voter guide).
Would 'remove unnecessary barriers to increasing supply' (housing) (ClickOrlando voter guide) - pro-housing-supply, so mixed with the smart-growth/home-rule entry.

Charles Burkett.quote_or_summary: 'Data centers must provide for their own power and water supplies' and 'should only be allowed in locations where a referendum vote of all the residents' approves them.
'Overdevelopment, overbuilding must be stopped.' 'Florida is full and must stop adding people to our state.' (Roster notes platform to stop 'Manhattanization'.)

Frank J. Russo.quote_or_summary: 'welcomes technology investments in the state for AI and data centers' (WLRN); 'Florida should embrace innovation without asking families to shoulder the cost'; wants large developments to pay for the infrastructure they need (ClickOrlando).
Supports 'encouraging responsible housing growth' and workforce housing; new large developments should pay for needed infrastructure. Press release lists him as a real estate developer.

Moliere \"Moe\" Dimanche.quote_or_summary: 'data centers will be banned' if he is governor.
'the state will not preempt local government when I take office' (local control); wants state to give abandoned properties to eligible Floridians for homesteading; would abolish HOAs.

Dean Ocean Abrams.quote_or_summary: WLRN summary says he 'opposes data centers'; the ClickOrlando guide says he did not respond - single-source, so treat as softer.

Scott Eckhard Jewett.quote_or_summary: Wants 'ensuring data centers do no harm' (WLRN); did not answer ClickOrlando's question.
Website: 'cut rules and fees that raise the price of food, housing, energy, insurance and hiring' (deregulatory; names no specific land rules).

Jose Javier Rodriguez.quote_or_summary: Says AG should 'defend local control and home rule' ('Home Rule Jose'); pledged to 'fight the sell or swap of conservation land' (ClickOrlando voter guide).
Campaign cost priority: 'protect taxpayers from data centers' (WLRN summary; no further detail).
Goal to 'fight any sale, swap, or surplus of Florida's public and conservation land'; also wants to 'rein in the utilities'.

James Uthmeier.quote_or_summary: No documented position found: did not answer ClickOrlando guide; guide found no public statements on state preemption of local governments. He proposed/built Alligator Alcatraz inside Big Cypress National Preserve (Everglades), July 2025 (Wikipedia).

No documented position found: WLRN says he describes no position on data centers/land use; a web search found no data-center-specific action by his office (he is running on child safety, immigration, Big Tech/AI, China ties).

Joey Mendoza Atkins.quote_or_summary: Supports a statewide moratorium; says he will fight to 'block and ban data centers' (WLRN).

'Joey will fight for family farms by protecting farmland from predatory developers'; wants Legislature to end the 'rent-a-cow' greenbelt loophole (WLRN). Own guide answer: 'Smart conservation and responsible land stewardship are not obstacles to economic growth.'

Wilton Simpson.quote_or_summary: Says 'residential development encroaches on our rural areas'; touts conservation easements (18,279.38 acres in May 2023) that 'will prevent future development of the land'; 'From preserving farmland to reducing regulatory burdens, these efforts are helping secure Florida's future.' Championed 2021 Florida Wildlife Corridor Act; prioritizes Rural and Family Lands Protection Program.

Also touts 'reducing regulatory burdens' and as Senate President helped pass the Right to Farm Act (legal shield for farm operations vs. neighbors) - farm-industry friendly, not anti-development per se. (Roster/prior research: DeSantis vetoed $100M for the Rural lands program per Capitolist coverage - not attributed to Simpson.)

WUWF interview: "Nobody cares for them or likes them"; says data centers are not much of his job as commissioner. If one is built: only in industrial parks, not on farmland or community commercial land; "zero fresh water" (reclaimed only); "they should have to generate 100 percent of their own electricity"; Legislature should "leave it in the hands of local governments." Conditional, not a moratorium.

On rural lands program (buys development rights from farmers): "We're accomplishing both things in the most affordable way" (protecting wildlife corridor and agriculture); says he put $300 million in the budget leaving the Senate and the Legislature later gave his agency $800 million over his first four years as commissioner. Campaign emphasizes conservation easements (Florida Trib).

Angie Nixon.quote_or_summary: Per Wikipedia, in September 2026 she supported a federal moratorium on new data center construction until regulatory safeguards protect communities and the environment (primary source not read).

Blaise Ingoglia.quote_or_summary: CONTEXT: homebuilder/developer (Hartland Homes, America One Mortgage, Spring Hill); no documented position on growth/land/data centers; his DOGE audits target local-government spending; guide lists 'housing and property insurance affordability' and eliminating homestead property taxes.

Tara Poulton.quote_or_summary: 'We really need to hit the brakes on growth and slow it down' (not stop it) to protect environment; enforce/strengthen environmental standards, keep wetland buffers; says she took no developer money; supports home rule; on Mosaic: 'Let's let them finish the job they've started' (no expansion).

Thomas Schwarz.quote_or_summary: Site lists 'Responsible and Sustainable City Growth', 'Environmental Protections', and 'Preserving Ward 3's Historic Character'; says growth requires sound infrastructure planning (vague, no specific votes).

Tampa Bay 28 questionnaire: most important issue is 'managing growth responsibly while ensuring our infrastructure and quality of life keep pace'; cites traffic, aging infrastructure, development pressure, neighborhood character; but 'Growth itself isn't the problem' - the challenge is planning and investing in infrastructure.

Kemp Schuessler.quote_or_summary: Site lists 'Smart Growth and Planning' and 'responsible growth' with road/drainage investment; no specifics.
City bio: 'longtime resident of the Wares Creek neighborhood'; 30+ years financial-services executive; appointed July 23 2025. Site lists 'Smart Growth and Planning'.

Keith J. Green.quote_or_summary: Site prioritizes infrastructure, drainage/flood prevention, public-private partnerships and 'encourage investment in Bradenton'; served four years on Bradenton Planning Commission; no stance on growth limits.

Tampa Bay 28: traffic needs 'practical, common-sense solutions' while 'planning responsibly for future growth'; public-private partnerships to fund improvements. Planning Commission member since 2022 (Vice Chair 2025).

Jim Boyd.quote_or_summary: Voted for SB 180 (2025), which restricts local governments in storm-affected counties from adopting more restrictive land-development rules; Senate passage 37-0 (Apr 9 2025) and concurrence 34-1 (May 2 2025). Prior research says the roll-call PDF shows 'Y Boyd-20'; the bill page I read gives tallies only, so Boyd's individual Yea was not re-confirmed by me. Manatee County is among local governments suing over the law (per prior research). Harvey Shifrin says SB 180 'prevented the county from banning large-scale data centers' (county commissioners' view).

Voted Yea on final Senate passage of HB 399 (2026, Land Use and Development Regulations: off-site-built homes permitted as of right, administrative approval for large destination resorts, permit-fee limits, compatibility factors), 27-11 on Mar 13 2026; voted Nay on the Jones floor amendment (per prior research). Bill summary and tallies verified on flsenate.gov; individual vote per prior research.

Bradenton Times endorsement of Baldi (opinion): Boyd 'has repeatedly voted to eliminate elements of home rule by supporting developer-driven preemption bills' (names SB 180 and 'SB 399'); says they left the current county commission unable to reverse the prior board's weakening of wetland protections. Editorial opinion, not Boyd's words.

Ocean Fitts.quote_or_summary: Wants to restore home rule, better protect wetlands and environmental resources, invest in infrastructure (Bradenton Times endorsement summary).

Jordan Varnadore.quote_or_summary: No documented positions on growth, development or data centers: his ballot profile lists only Economy, Education, Guns; he declined the Bradenton Times interview, which predicted he would be 'a reliable vote for the developer-influenced RPOF machine' (editorial opinion, not his words). Platform from prior research: reduce burdensome regulations.

Kelly Kirschner.quote_or_summary: Opposes proposed hyperscale data centers near Arcadia and Fort Meade; says AI companies 'need to be held liable'; says no federal framework guides these decisions (Tampa Bay Times/WUSF forum coverage).
Says he helped build Payne Park and stopped a developer from putting 10-story condos into a single-family neighborhood (his own claim, as reported by WGCU).

Sydney Gruters.quote_or_summary: 'Big Tech should pay their own way. They have the money.' Energy and water costs should not fall on consumers and local communities should decide whether data centers are built; she did not say whether the DeSoto project should be approved.
Her website says she will 'fight to curb overdevelopment and keep homeownership within reach for working families' (as quoted by WGCU; vague, no specific policy).

Harvey Shifrin.quote_or_summary: 'I am not against thoughtful development, but the planning must be the prerogative of the county'; wants home rule returned to counties ('Local politics should stay local'); says SB 180 blocks Manatee from stricter wetland buffers/setbacks; wants Live Local changes that respect comp plans; opposes Amendment 3.
States no personal position; cites county commissioners' view that SB 180 'prevented the county from banning large-scale data centers'.

Bill Conerly.quote_or_summary: Supports the Live Local Act's goal of attainable housing but backs targeted reforms; 'We can increase Florida's housing supply while protecting property rights'; 'We don't have to choose between protecting our environment and supporting a strong economy'; backs Amendment 3. Data centers: not addressed.

Nick Pachota.quote_or_summary: 'I would repeal Live Local and restore local control of growth/land use decisions.' 'Live Local has failed to increase supply of affordable housing units in Sarasota County.' Data centers: not addressed.

Ryan Neill.quote_or_summary: 'I support changes to the Live Local Act. In fact I support its repeal.' 'local counties and planning boards have a better idea of what should be built in their communities.' Data centers: not addressed.

Lisa Klein.quote_or_summary: 'Our local governments need the authority to address flooding and guide development based on their communities' needs.' 'Live Local has pre-empted local governments in ways that make collaboration difficult' - would keep working provisions. Data centers: not addressed.

Sari Lindroos-Valimaki.quote_or_summary: 'I am very much against placing them in places they should not be placed'; thinks Florida is not the place for data centers except maybe north Florida; wants comp plan to define hyperscale AI data centers with a specific zoning category; fears water pollution, grid drain, few jobs; asked commissioners June 4 not to submit comp plan to the state.

'Once the land is gone, it's gone' (farmland/food security); build roads before houses; protect water quality; opposes Mosaic phosphate mining operations. But also says 'growth can't be stopped, so planning for it matters more than opposing it.'

Elizabeth \"Liz\" Arnold.quote_or_summary: Says county has 'a lot of overdevelopment', 65,000 homes in the pipeline, suggests pausing new projects; wants to protect farms, ranches, small business; 'Things could slow down to give District 1 a break'; credits a decade of activism with helping stop subdivisions and save a canopy road; has fought for the Future Development Area Boundary.

No documented personal position on data centers (Observer and Beacons articles do not report one). Manatee County commission as a whole unanimously approved a one-year data-center moratorium on Oct 8 2026.

Amanda Ballard.quote_or_summary: Sitting commissioner. Manatee commissioners 'unanimously approved' a one-year moratorium on new data center projects (Oct 8 2026); the article names no individual commissioners, so her own vote is inferred from unanimity, not stated.

Prior research (source not re-verified): Oct 5 2023 voted with majority to cut local wetland buffers to state minimums (tally differs between outlets; buffers restored 2025); Feb 18 2026 voted yes on 5-2 vote giving Mosaic a 14-year Four Corners mine plan extension ('difficult decision'). Same research credits her with spearheading the Mixon Fruit Farms land purchase (county conservation-type purchase). Observer (Aug 2026): she said 'we've been kind of limited by the state'. Observer editorial recommended her for 'defense of individual liberty'.

Michael Owen.quote_or_summary: Per prior research, voted Yea on SB 180 (2025, House 115-1 on Apr 29; concurrence 106-0 May 2) and on HB 399 (2026 Land Use and Development Regulations; House 71-38 on Mar 3 and concurrence 73-27 on Mar 13), both of which limit local land-use authority. HB 399 summary and tallies verified; his individual votes not re-confirmed. Real estate attorney.

Gerald Baldi.quote_or_summary: Campaign site: 'Ensuring growth benefits residents, not special interests'; 'Safeguarding our coastlines, reefs, wetlands, and wildlife.' BallotReady: 'Infrastructure, First!!! Impact Studies, District Approval before any new home building.' Endorsed by Bradenton Times and Environmental Caucus of Florida. Nothing found on data centers.

Lisa Gonzalez Moore.quote_or_summary: Tampa Bay 28: ties downtown redevelopment and workforce growth to infrastructure investment, 'fiscal planning' and 'long term growth of our City'; goal of a more vibrant downtown (pro-redevelopment, urban-core framing).

donalds_investors.words: NOT FOUND as 'investors'. Only a secondhand claim: a Reddit post (via the scraper site reddit.sentinel-team.org) says James Fishback, Donalds' primary rival, obtained video of a private Donalds event in Pensacola where guests were told to become 'shareholders' in Byron's company, to 'help steer the direction of Florida'; Fishback: "Unlike Byron, I don't have shareholders. I only work for you." The word 'investors' does not appear.
donalds_investors.reported_by: Reddit post paraphrasing James Fishback; no news outlet found; video not linked

notes: DONALDS DATA CENTERS: owner's belief is PARTLY supported. June 2025 he said data centers and power are the state's future and 'embrace that'; voted for the 10-yr state AI-regulation moratorium (May 2025); opposes a statewide data-center moratorium (July 2026). But by Sept-Oct 2026 he moved toward 'local governments can say no', backs SB 484 and filed a federal ratepayer bill. Jolly accuses him of shifting because positions are 'politically unpopular'. 'Develop' (land) not documented: no Donalds quote on farmland/land-use found; only economic-growth statements.
Donalds 'investors' claim could not be verified; searches surfaced only Fishback's 'slave to donors' remarks (Nov 2025) and fundraiser-price reporting ($50,000 a plate Mar-a-Lago dinner May 1).
Governor minors: Dimanche, Abrams, Jewett, Datto, Russo birthplace/upbringing not found in any source read (WLRN, ClickOrlando, Wikipedia). Datto did not answer any guide.

P1 statewide: Taddeo, Moody, Gillespie, Uthmeier data-center/land positions NOT documented in any source read. Roots for Uthmeier, Moody, Nixon from Wikipedia (birthplace + high school). Bellamy 'born in Bradenton' is from prior roster research; fifth-generation confirmed by Bradenton Times endorsement.
Observer candidate Q&A profiles (yourobserver.com/news/2026/oct/...) exist for HD72, HD73, HD74 and school board - they give growth positions but rarely birthplace.
